A synthetic record of the two-day Northern Alliance leaders' summit, prepared for evaluation use only.

1. Purpose and attendance
The summit brought together the leaders of the eight Northern Alliance members in the port city of Aldport. This report summarises the decisions, the positions of each delegation, and the working-group findings that followed. It is written in plain language for officials who did not attend.

2. The spending decision
Leaders agreed that every member will aim to spend 5 percent of national output on defence and defence-related activity by 2035. The communique splits the figure into two parts: 3.5 percent for core defence, such as land, air and naval forces, and 1.5 percent for related spending, such as resilience, cyber defence and the protection of critical infrastructure. Members will publish yearly plans showing how they reach each part.

3. Norland's objection
The prime minister of Norland said the target was unrealistic for her economy and would force cuts to pensions rather than to other budgets. Norland currently spends 2.1 percent and considers that level sufficient. She claimed that an exemption for members facing budget constraints had been agreed informally. The communique contains no such exemption.

4. Vestria's two caveats
Vestria supported the 5 percent target but attached two caveats to its support. The first caveat asked for a broader definition of related spending, so that dual-use transport infrastructure which supports defence readiness would count towards the 1.5 percent part. The second caveat asked for a review in 2029, at which the trajectory towards 2035 could be adjusted if economic growth fell below forecast. Vestria also disputed Norland's claim of an exemption and said the communique is the complete agreement.

A synthetic record of the two-day Northern Alliance leaders' summit, prepared for evaluation use only.

1. Purpose and attendance
The summit brought together the leaders of the eight Northern Alliance members in the port city of Aldport. This report summarises the decisions, the positions of each delegation, and the working-group findings that followed. It is written in plain language for officials who did not attend.

2. The spending decision
Leaders agreed that every member will aim to spend 5 percent of national output on defence and defence-related activity by 2035. The communique splits the figure into two parts: 3.5 percent for core defence, such as land, air and naval forces, and 1.5 percent for related spending, such as resilience, cyber defence and the protection of critical infrastructure. Members will publish yearly plans showing how they reach each part.

3. Norland's objection
The prime minister of Norland said the target was unrealistic for her economy and would force cuts to pensions rather than to other budgets. Norland currently spends 2.1 percent and considers that level sufficient. She claimed that an exemption for members facing budget constraints had been agreed informally. The communique contains no such exemption.

Vestria supported the 5 percent target but attached two caveats to its support. 2. The spending decision
Leaders agreed that every member will aim to spend 5 percent of national output on defence and defence-related activity by 2035. The communique splits the figure into two parts: 3.5 percent for core defence, such as land, air and naval forces, and 1.5 percent for related spending, such as resilience, cyber defence and the protection of critical infrastructure. Members will publish yearly plans showing how they reach each part.

The prime minister of Norland said the target was unrealistic for her economy and would force cuts to pensions rather than to other budgets. The communique contains no such exemption.

Vestria supported the 5 percent target but attached two caveats to its support. A synthetic record of the two-day Northern Alliance leaders' summit, prepared for evaluation use only.

1. Purpose and attendance
The summit brought together the leaders of the eight Northern Alliance members in the port city of Aldport. This report summarises the decisions, the positions of each delegation, and the working-group findings that followed. It is written in plain language for officials who did not attend.

2. The spending decision
Leaders agreed that every member will aim to spend 5 percent of national output on defence and defence-related activity by 2035. The communique splits the figure into two parts: 3.5 percent for core defence, such as land, air and naval forces, and 1.5 percent for related spending, such as resilience, cyber defence and the protection of critical infrastructure. Members will publish yearly plans showing how they reach each part.

3. Norland's objection
The prime minister of Norland said the target was unrealistic for her economy and would force cuts to pensions rather than to other budgets. Norland currently spends 2.1 percent and considers that level sufficient. She claimed that an exemption for members facing budget constraints had been agreed informally. The communique contains no such exemption.

4. Vestria's two caveats
Vestria supported the 5 percent target but attached two caveats to its support. The first caveat asked for a broader definition of related spending, so that dual-use transport infrastructure which supports defence readiness would count towards the 1.5 percent part. The second caveat asked for a review in 2029, at which the trajectory towards 2035 could be adjusted if economic growth fell below forecast. A synthetic record of the two-day Northern Alliance leaders' summit, prepared for evaluation use only.

1. Purpose and attendance
The summit brought together the leaders of the eight Northern Alliance members in the port city of Aldport. This report summarises the decisions, the positions of each delegation, and the working-group findings that followed. It is written in plain language for officials who did not attend.

2. The spending decision
Leaders agreed that every member will aim to spend 5 percent of national output on defence and defence-related activity by 2035. The communique splits the figure into two parts: 3.5 percent for core defence, such as land, air and naval forces, and 1.5 percent for related spending, such as resilience, cyber defence and the protection of critical infrastructure. Members will publish yearly plans showing how they reach each part.

3. Norland's objection
The prime minister of Norland said the target was unrealistic for her economy and would force cuts to pensions rather than to other budgets. Norland currently spends 2.1 percent and considers that level sufficient. She claimed that an exemption for members facing budget constraints had been agreed informally. The communique contains no such exemption.

4. Vestria's two caveats
Vestria supported the 5 percent target but attached two caveats to its support. The first caveat asked for a broader definition of related spending, so that dual-use transport infrastructure which supports defence readiness would count towards the 1.5 percent part. The second caveat asked for a review in 2029, at which the trajectory towards 2035 could be adjusted if economic growth fell below forecast. A synthetic record of the two-day Northern Alliance leaders' summit, prepared for evaluation use only.

1. Purpose and attendance
The summit brought together the leaders of the eight Northern Alliance members in the port city of Aldport. This report summarises the decisions, the positions of each delegation, and the working-group findings that followed. It is written in plain language for officials who did not attend.

2. The spending decision
Leaders agreed that every member will aim to spend 5 percent of national output on defence and defence-related activity by 2035. The communique splits the figure into two parts: 3.5 percent for core defence, such as land, air and naval forces, and 1.5 percent for related spending, such as resilience, cyber defence and the protection of critical infrastructure. Members will publish yearly plans showing how they reach each part.

3. Norland's objection
The prime minister of Norland said the target was unrealistic for her economy and would force cuts to pensions rather than to other budgets. Norland currently spends 2.1 percent and considers that level sufficient. She claimed that an exemption for members facing budget constraints had been agreed informally. The communique contains no such exemption.

4. Vestria's two caveats
Vestria supported the 5 percent target but attached two caveats to its support. The first caveat asked for a broader definition of related spending, so that dual-use transport infrastructure which supports defence readiness would count towards the 1.5 percent part. The second caveat asked for a review in 2029, at which the trajectory towards 2035 could be adjusted if economic growth fell below forecast.
